learning: If max_error on s-bend and slalom falls below about 0.05 while steering_oscillation stays near 0.2, keep the wider array and try a slightly higher base_speed. If oscillation rises sharply, return kp to 2.5 and kd to 0.4. If line_loss_events remain 1.0 on bends, the outer sensors are not seeing the tape, so check the sensor size or y position in the next iteration.
notes: Complete robot on the Builder's widened 7-sensor array at ±0.06 m, with kp raised to 3.0, kd to 0.5 and base_speed lowered to 1.7 for stronger, slower bend correction. Based on iteration 1 (s-bend and slalom line losses of 1.0 per run, max_error about 0.06) and the oval finish time of 1.73 s.
rationale: Race evidence: iteration 1 (score 337.6) finished 17 of 20 oval runs, up from 3 of 20. Both s-bend and slalom still end off track, with max_error about 0.061 and 0.060 at the 0.06 m limit, and line_loss_events of 1.0 per run on both. Narrowing the track and raising the wheel radius (iteration 0 to 1) left s-bend progress flat at about 0.24, so turn authority alone is not the limit. The Builder's wider 7-sensor array at ±0.06 m keeps the tape visible and the signal graded out to the limit, which addresses the line-loss and saturation evidence. I kept the Builder's geometry as proposed. Sensor weights are scaled to x (33.3*x, so ±2 at the outer sensors) to keep the signal range the same as the ±0.03 m design, which had weights of ±2 at ±0.03 m. The Builder's expected change is the array span. For the controller, I raise kp from 2.5 to 3.0 so the correction on bends is stronger with the outer sensors reporting earlier, and I raise kd from 0.4 to 0.5 to damp the extra gain. I lower base_speed from 1.8 to 1.7 because the s-bend and slalom fail by drifting outward and slower bends give the controller more time to recover. The oval mean finish of 1.73 s (iteration 1) leaves room under 3 s. line_loss stays at last_direction. Expected result: fewer off-track ends on s-bend and slalom and max_error below about 0.05, with oscillation possibly rising because of the higher kp and kd. The next race will show whether that happened.
